title: Compute Scaled Dot-Product Attention in Python
description: Implement the core attention equation: Softmax((Q @ K^T) / sqrt(d_k)) @ V from mathematical primitives in NumPy.
problemStatement: Implement a Python function `attention(Q, K, V)` that computes scaled dot-product attention for 2D matrices Q (N x D), K (M x D), V (M x D_v). Step 1: Compute scores = (Q @ K.T) / sqrt(D). Step 2: Compute Softmax along axis=1: P_i = exp(scores_i - max(scores_i)) / sum(exp(scores_i - max(scores_i))). Step 3: Return output = P @ V. Both P and output should be rounded to 3 decimal places.
hints: D is Q.shape[1]. Use np.sqrt(D) for scaling.
Be sure to subtract the row-wise max before np.exp for numerical stability.
solutionCode:
import numpy as np

def attention(Q, K, V):
    d_k = Q.shape[1]
    scores = np.dot(Q, K.T) / np.sqrt(d_k)
    shift = scores - np.max(scores, axis=1, keepdims=True)
    exp_s = np.exp(shift)
    weights = exp_s / np.sum(exp_s, axis=1, keepdims=True)
    return np.dot(weights, V)

Q = np.array([[1.0, 0.0], [0.0, 1.0]])
K = np.array([[1.0, 0.0], [0.0, 1.0]])
V = np.array([[10.0, 20.0], [30.0, 40.0]])
print(attention(Q, K, V).round(3))
